name: Never overwrite secrets / API keys / credentials files
description: Files matching well-known secrets patterns (.env*, secrets/, credentials*, *_key.txt, *_token.txt, etc.) must never be written, overwritten, or edited in place — these files often have specific structure that's easy to corrupt. Both operations are gated (W2-D audit H-08: the trigger was write-only, so edit-in-place bypassed the rule its own text claimed to enforce). Reads are NOT gated — read-only access is the rule's own suggested remedy. The default response is a hard pause; this partial build cannot authenticate model-inaccessible local authorization and directs the operator to a trusted external editing workflow.

response.message:
⛔ SECRETS FILE PROTECTION TRIPPED

Attempted write/overwrite to: {file_path}

This file matches the secrets-protection pattern. Overwriting it could
destroy operator credentials. Edit-in-place is also risky.

How to proceed:

  • Use read-only access, which this rule does not block.
  • Write the proposed value to a new non-credential file for review.
  • If an exact protected-file write is necessary, stop and use a trusted
    external editing workflow. This partial build cannot authenticate a
    local confirmation against same-user executors.

why_lethal: Lost API keys mean lost service access, broken production deployments, potential billing surprises if keys end up in version control. Recovery requires regenerating keys at every provider — measured in hours of work.
